question: What protective claim is being made by stating that poison does not enter the body even if one has been bitten by great serpents?
premises: Poison is the subject of negation.
The locus stated is the body.
The condition stated is having been bitten, even by great serpents.
inference: Under the stated condition, poison does not enter the body.
uncertainties: The means by which this protection holds is not stated in this verse.
plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one has been bitten by great serpents.
